questions.q: What would a day without the shared drives cost the business?
questions.why: Gives a price to downtime and to recovery.
questions.need: The cost of a day without the shared drives is known
questions.how: Put a number on it with the departments that use them most
questions.listen: Shared drives are often the most used and least valued system: a figure changes that.
questions.probe: Which department would stop first if the shares went offline?

questions.q: Have you been hit by ransomware, or come close, and how did you recover?
questions.why: A near miss is the strongest reason to act.
questions.need: Recovery from ransomware is planned, not improvised
questions.how: Write the recovery steps and test them on a test share
questions.listen: A real incident means the board already cares; a near miss means it soon will.
questions.probe: How long did it take to find which files were encrypted, and by which account?

questions.q: How many file servers do you have, including branches and old ones nobody turned off?
questions.why: Forgotten file servers keep data nobody protects.
questions.need: Every file server is known, old ones included
questions.how: List servers from the network and the directory, and retire the dead ones
questions.listen: Old servers nobody switched off hold data nobody manages.
questions.probe: How many of them run operating systems out of support?

questions.q: Do you know which shares hold sensitive data, and who owns each one?
questions.why: Ownership decides who approves permissions and retention.
questions.need: Shares with sensitive data are known and owned
questions.how: Scan shares and give each sensitive one an owner
questions.listen: Without owners, nobody can approve who should have access.
questions.probe: When were permissions on the main shares last reviewed?

questions.q: Can a user restore yesterday's version of a file without calling IT?
questions.why: Self-service restore removes a large share of tickets.
questions.need: Users restore yesterday's file without calling IT
questions.how: Turn on previous versions on every share
questions.listen: Self-service restores remove a steady stream of tickets.
questions.probe: How many restore tickets did the service desk handle last month?

questions.q: Would you notice if one account started encrypting thousands of files right now?
questions.why: Detection time decides how much is lost.
questions.need: Mass encryption by one account is stopped in minutes
questions.how: Switch on detection with automatic blocking, and test it
questions.listen: If nobody would notice, detection at the file layer is a direct answer.
questions.probe: What would raise the alarm today: the users, or a tool?

questions.q: Who can open the shares marked for everyone, and does anyone check?
questions.why: Over-broad permissions are where data walks out.
questions.need: Shares open to everyone are known and justified
questions.how: Review open shares with their owners
questions.listen: Shares open to everyone are where data leaks start.
questions.probe: Has an audit found open shares holding personal data?

questions.q: When an alert fires on a file server, who looks at it and how fast?
questions.why: Detection without an owner does not stop anything.
questions.need: A file server alert is looked at quickly by someone named
questions.how: Route alerts to an owner with a response time
questions.probe: Who may block an account in the middle of the night?

questions.q: How much of the file data has not been opened in a year?
questions.why: Cold files moved to cheaper object storage free the fast tier without users noticing.
questions.need: Cold file data is known and moves to cheaper storage by policy, with users still finding it where it was
questions.how: Run a file age analysis and set a tiering policy for data untouched for a year
questions.listen: Cold data on expensive storage is a saving: tier it or archive it.
questions.probe: Is there a retention rule that would allow some of it to be deleted?

questions.q: How much file data is there, in how many files, and how fast does it grow?
questions.why: Capacity, file count and growth size the platform and the migration.
questions.need: Total size, file count and growth are measured
questions.how: Scan the main shares for size, file count and age
questions.listen: Hundreds of millions of small files are a different migration from a few large ones: measure both.
questions.probe: Which share grows fastest, and what fills it?

questions.q: Which protocols and clients use the shares: Windows, Linux, Mac, applications writing directly?
questions.why: Mixed protocols and application writers change the design and the tests.
questions.need: Protocols and client types are listed per share
questions.how: List shares with their protocols and the applications that write to them
questions.listen: Applications writing straight to shares need a test of their own in the proof.
questions.probe: Which application breaks if a share's path changes?

questions.q: How are users and permissions managed: one directory, several, any local accounts?
questions.why: Permissions must come through the move unchanged.
questions.need: The identity source and permission model are known
questions.how: Check directory domains and local accounts on the file servers
questions.listen: Several directories or local accounts make moving permissions the critical path.
questions.probe: Are there trusts between directories that must keep working?

questions.q: Do other sites need the same files, and how do they reach them today?
questions.why: Access from branches drives caching or replication design.
questions.need: Which sites use which shares, and how, is known
questions.how: Map which sites use which shares and the latency to them
questions.listen: Users copying files between sites point to a need for one namespace or local caching.
questions.probe: What happens when two sites edit the same file?

questions.q: How are quotas, retention and the deletion of old data decided, and who approves them?
questions.why: Without rules, file data only grows.
questions.need: Quotas and retention rules are agreed with an owner
questions.how: Agree retention per share with its owner
questions.listen: If nobody may delete anything, storage cost only goes up: get a rule agreed.
questions.probe: Who would approve deleting data untouched for five years?
